title: psf-os: a self-checking layer between a user's circuit and an IBM heavy-hex device, without the calibration map
description: psf-os places a circuit by formula (a ring by the rule, a 2D circuit by translation of its own pattern), adds checks made of the user's own circuit to the same job (a floor, a mirror, a ring sentinel), keeps a list of what it found dead, and returns an answer card. It does not read a calibration quality number: it uses the coupling graph and the elements marked as failed. Version 0.2 adds real-time control: circuits that measure in the middle and act on the result while they run, each with its uncontrolled twin (the off arm) and a floor in the same job; conditions on a whole classical register; build rules taken from what the devices did (fixed circuits packed together, conditional items kept apart, the build environment recorded); and a loop of rounds that diagnoses the device, applies a fixed rule and runs the chosen circuit unattended, with a ledger keyed to the device record's calibration time stamp. Version 0.3 parks a qubit that waits in |1> in |0> for the wait by default (checked at every build: the noiseless output and the compiled CZ count unchanged), adds a loop that decides inside one job (the incumbent and the candidate side by side) and the replay of a recorded night, and records the qubits holding a superposition at every wait. Version 0.3.1 also parks, by default, a waiting qubit that is more likely in |1> than in |0> (entangled ones included), behind a fence on that qubit and the wait's own qubits only; on the RUS chains it kept +0.097 and +0.025 more than 0.3.0's default in the same job. The declared device tests behind it are in https://github.com/TN-Holdings-LLC/psf-os-lab-notebook.
